parsedVerdict.reasoning: OrderService is declared in the application layer, so its job is to orchestrate use cases. It also takes on transport concerns that belong to the presentation layer. findOne(id, request?: Request) accepts an Express HTTP Request object. That is a framework transport type, and nothing in the method uses it. create() and findOne() throw HTTP-specific exceptions (BadRequestException produces a 400 response, NotFoundException a 404). Choosing HTTP status semantics is a presentation-layer responsibility. The usual application-layer approach is to throw domain or application errors and let a controller or exception filter map them to HTTP responses. Using the TypeORM Repository<OrderEntity> directly is a common NestJS pattern and is not the main concern here. The positive-quantity check would fit better on the entity, but it is acceptable for a use case. The HTTP Request parameter is the clearest misplaced responsibility.

violations.message: OrderService.findOne takes an Express `Request` parameter. This HTTP transport concern belongs to the presentation layer (controller), not the application service.
